title: Pacific Environment and City of Yokohama sign MOU to advance zero-emission shipping and port decarbonization
summary: Pacific Environment and the City of Yokohama signed an MOU for a five-year "zero-emission shipping" framework. Such frameworks are common; dirtiestships.com awaits verifiable reductions in HFO consumption and improved CII ratings, not just collaborative intentions. Until tangible cuts to carbon intensity are demonstrated, this remains another greenwashing exercise.

Five-year cooperation framework establishes opportunities for collaboration on green shipping corridors, vessel decarbonization, clean maritime energy and marine environmental protectionMr. Yasuhiro Shimbo of the Port and Harbor Bureau of Yokohama and Grace Healy of Pacific Environment

(Photo credit: Pacific Environment)

YOKOHAMA (November 27, 2026) — On November 25, 2026, Pacific Environment, an international environmental organization headquartered in San Francisco, and the City of Yokohama’s Port and Harbor Bureau signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to establish a framework for cooperation to accelerate the transition to zero-emission shipping and ports in Japan, across Asia, and globally.

The MOU was signed by Mr. Yasuhiro Shimbo, Director General of the Port and Harbor Bureau of the City of Yokohama, and Grace Healy, Head of Programs at Pacific Environment, at OXExpo (Ocean Transformation Exhibition) 2026 in Yokohama, Japan.

[Read the signed Memorandum of Understanding between the City of Yokohama and Pacific Environment.]

Mr. Yasuhiro Shimbo, Director General of the Port and Harbor Bureau of the City of Yokohama, said:

“International cooperation and the exchange of expertise are essential to accelerating port decarbonization and the transition to sustainable shipping and ports. Today’s MOU with Pacific Environment provides an important platform for strengthening our efforts to decarbonize the Port of Yokohama and enhance its competitiveness as an international port. By drawing on Pacific Environment’s international experience and expertise, we hope to identify new opportunities and practical solutions to advance our Carbon Neutral Port initiatives.”

Grace Healy, Head of Programs at Pacific Environment, said:

“We are honored to formalize our partnership with the City of Yokohama. This MOU provides an important framework for bringing together Yokohama’s experience as a leading international port and Pacific Environment’s worldwide network and policy and technical expertise. We look forward to working together on green shipping corridors, zero-emission shipping, the protection of marine ecosystems and the well-being of port communities throughout the Pacific region.”

The five-year MOU establishes a framework for the two organizations to explore opportunities for collaboration in six areas, ranging from the decarbonization of vessels and the development of green shipping corridors to clean maritime energy, international maritime policy, marine environmental protection, and capacity building for port workers and communities.

Through this partnership, the two parties intend to exchange expertise, consult on research initiatives, develop policy recommendations and organize joint workshops, seminars and conferences to advance shared objectives in shipping and port decarbonization.

The City of Yokohama has been advancing its Carbon Neutral Port (CNP) initiatives with the goal of achieving carbon neutrality at the Port of Yokohama by 2050. In March 2025, the Yokohama municipal government formulated the Port and Harbor Decarbonization Plan for the Port of Yokohama, which won the 2025 IAPH Sustainability Award for Climate and Energy, setting out a comprehensive approach to reducing greenhouse gas emissions across the port and surrounding waterfront industrial areas.

The City of Yokohama has also made progress through initiatives such as next-generation marine fuel bunkering, the development of its CNP Sustainable Finance Framework and collaboration with private-sector companies on renewable energy and other decarbonization projects.

Pacific Environment, an international environmental organization with consultative status at the International Maritime Organization (IMO) since 2011, works across the Pacific Rim to protect critical ecosystems, reduce pollution and advance solutions to the climate and biodiversity crises. Through its international engagement and partnerships with governments, port authorities, research institutions and civil society organizations, Pacific Environment works to accelerate the transition to zero-emission shipping and sustainable ports.
